title: doctor prints its summary last and spends 55% of its bytes repeating four remedy sentences
body:
`doctor`'s text output computes the orienting information and prints it last, then spends 55% of its bytes repeating four sentences.

**Measured in Lamplight, 2026-08-28, on a store with 353 threads and 173 findings.** Filed from there rather than fixed in place: every Intent node was active at the time and this is a presentation change to a shared command.

**Nothing here is a missing capability.** The census exists, the classes exist, the advisory accounting exists, and `--format json` already emits all of it structured. This is entirely about where the text renderer puts what it already has.

## What it does now

    $ intent doctor | wc -lc
    348 lines, 70474 bytes

346 of those lines are `residue:` / `remedy:` pairs in artefact order. Then, on the last two lines:

    advisory: 2 note(s) not shown and not counted -- `intent doctor --verbose` reads them
    doctor: 173 finding(s) across 353 thread(s), 5 issue(s), 2575 view(s), 5975 file(s) -- 2 advisory(ies), not counted

**That summary line is good, and it is line 348 of 348.** It answers "how much of this is there and what is it about", which is the question a reader has BEFORE the wall of findings, not after it. I twice mis-read this command's behaviour while writing this issue -- first as having no summary at all, then as silently dropping the advisory class -- and both mistakes came from reading the top of the output, which is where the orienting line is not. A summary a reader has to scroll past 346 lines to reach is doing the work of a footer, and the information in it is not footer information.

## The repetition, measured

    remedy lines       39708 bytes
    distinct remedies    974 bytes  (4 sentences)
    -> repetition      38734 bytes  = 55% of the whole output

One remedy is printed 91 times and another 68 times. They are well-written sentences -- the status/gate one in particular carries a real ruling about not reaching for `wp done` -- and none of that survives being read for the ninety-first time. The remedy is a property of the CLASS, and it is being printed per ROW.

## The concentration is invisible, and it is the whole story

Grouping the same 173 findings by class, off `--format json`:

     91  model-inconsistent        [ST0356 alone: 61]
     68  status-gate-disagreement  [ST0288 alone: 9]
     13  attachment-drift
      1  view-skew

**61 of the 91 model-inconsistent findings are one thread, and 62 of them are one shape** (an AC naming a WP its thread does not have). The flat rendering cannot say that, so a reader meets 91 separate problems where there are approximately three, one of which is a single scope decision on a single thread.

This matters beyond readability. The estate treated this number as a workload for weeks. Rendered by class it is legible in one screen as: one held scope call, one known data defect awaiting a re-run, and one rename that has not been synced.

## What would fix it

Ordered by value, all of it rearrangement of data the command already has:

1. **Print the summary first as well as last**, or first instead of last.
2. **Group findings by class**, with a count per class.
3. **Print each distinct remedy once per class**, not once per row.
4. **Name the concentration** where one artefact dominates a class -- `[ST0356: 61 of 91]`. The json has `file` on every finding, so this is a count.

A `--group` flag would do, but the flat form is unlikely to be what anyone wants by default: it is the same content at 70KB instead of about 2KB.

## Not asked for, and deliberately

No change to what is detected, to the classes, to the exit status, or to `--format json`, which is already the right shape -- the grouped view above was produced from it in a dozen lines, which is the evidence that nothing needs computing that is not already computed.

**Practice this is an instance of: a summary is orienting information or it is not, and where it is printed decides which.** The same line at the top and the bottom of this output is two different features.
